[Sat 2026-05-09 08:41 UTC] Develop a script that performs intensive mathematical operations in parallel loops.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# parallel_math.sh — CPU-intensive parallel math loops
# Usage: ./parallel_math.sh [seconds] [workers]
# Example: ./parallel_math.sh 15 "$(nproc)"

set -euo pipefail

DURATION="${1:-10}"
WORKERS="${2:-$(nproc)}"

worker() {
  local id="$1"
  local end=$((SECONDS + DURATION))
  local iters=0

  # Math-heavy inner loop (integer ops + a bit of pseudo-random mixing)
  local x=$((id * 1103515245 + 12345))
  while (( SECONDS < end )); do
    for ((i=0; i<200000; i++)); do
      x=$(( (x * 48271) ^ (x >> 13) ^ (x << 7) ))
      x=$(( x & 0x7fffffff ))
      iters=$((iters + 1))
    done
  done

  printf "worker=%d iters=%d checksum=%d\n" "$id" "$iters" "$x"
}

echo "Running ${WORKERS} workers for ${DURATION}s (host logical cores: $(nproc))"

pids=()
for ((w=0; w<WORKERS; w++)); do
  worker "$w" &
  pids+=("$!")
done

for pid in "${pids[@]}"; do
  wait "$pid"
done
```

Save as `parallel_math.sh`, then:
```bash
chmod +x parallel_math.sh
./parallel_math.sh 10 "$(nproc)"
```

content.text:
Your script didn’t run: it has a typo—`Done` (capital D) should be `done`, which caused the “unexpected end of file” syntax error.

Fix + run (this will peg all logical cores during the run):

```bash
sed -i 's/^Done$/done/' parallel_math.sh
./parallel_math.sh 60 "$(nproc)"
```

If you truly want it to stay at ~100% CPU “until you stop it”, run a long duration and interrupt:

```bash
./parallel_math.sh 86400 "$(nproc)"   # Ctrl+C to stop
```
